summary: Design forecast triggers, pre-agreed financing and early-action protocols for humanitarian crises. Explore the practical five-day course.
lede: Anticipatory action links forecast evidence and pre-agreed financing to steps taken before a predictable shock causes severe harm. For humanitarian programme managers, disaster-risk officers and early-warning analysts, the training supports designing trigger-action protocols that connect forecasts to early assistance. You will assess hazard and exposure data, calibrate thresholds against forecast confidence, and map activation, financing and delivery responsibilities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who connect hazard information to humanitarian decisions, financing and delivery.
audience: Food-Security Analysts using IPC evidence to inform
prerequisites: Working familiarity with humanitarian programming, disaster-risk management, early-warning analysis or emergency planning is expected. No coding or programming is required.
